\label{lemma-compare-det}
Let $R$ be a local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ and
residue field $\kappa$. Let $M$ be a finite length $R$-module
which is annihilated by $\mathfrak m$. Let $l = \dim_\kappa(M)$.
Then the map
$$
\det\nolimits_\kappa(M) \longrightarrow \wedge^l_\kappa(M),
\quad
[e_1, \ldots, e_l] \longmapsto e_1 \wedge \ldots \wedge e_l
$$
is an isomorphism.
statement:
Let $(R,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$ be a local ring and $M$ a finite-length $R$-module of length $\ell$. An admissible sequence is an $\ell$-tuple $(e_1,\ldots,e_\ell)$ with $\mathfrak m e_i\subseteq\sum_{j<i}Re_j$. The determinant line $\det_\kappa(M)$ is the $\kappa$-space generated by symbols $[e_1,\ldots,e_\ell]$ modulo: (i) a symbol is zero if any $e_i\in\sum_{j<i}Re_j$; (ii) replacing $e_i$ by $\lambda e_i'+x$ with $x\in\sum_{j<i}Re_j$ and $\lambda\in R^\times$ scales the symbol by $\bar\lambda$; (iii) exchanging adjacent $e_{i-1},e_i$ changes the sign when $\mathfrak m e_i\subseteq\sum_{j<i-1}Re_j$. This line is one-dimensional. An isomorphism $h:M\to N$ induces $\det_\kappa(h)$ by applying $h$ to admissible symbols. For a short exact sequence $0\to K\to L\to N\to0$, the canonical determinant isomorphism $\gamma_{K\to L\to N}:\det_\kappa K\otimes_\kappa\det_\kappa N\xrightarrow{\sim}\det_\kappa L$ concatenates an admissible sequence of $K$ with chosen lifts of one from $N$; it is natural under isomorphisms of exact sequences.

\label{lemma-determinant-quotient-ring}
Let $(R', \mathfrak m') \to (R, \mathfrak m)$ be a local ring
homomorphism which induces an isomorphism on residue fields $\kappa$.
Then for every finite length $R$-module the restriction $M_{R'}$
is a finite length $R'$-module and there is a canonical isomorphism
$$
\det\nolimits_{R, \kappa}(M)
\longrightarrow
\det\nolimits_{R', \kappa}(M_{R'})
$$
This isomorphism is functorial in $M$ and compatible with the
isomorphisms $\gamma_{K \to L \to M}$ of Lemma \ref{lemma-det-exact-sequences}
defined for $\det_{R, \kappa}$ and $\det_{R', \kappa}$.

\label{lemma-times-u-determinant}
Let $R$ be a local ring with residue field $\kappa$.
Let $u \in R^*$ be a unit.
Let $M$ be a module of finite length over $R$.
Denote $u_M : M \to M$ the map multiplication by $u$.
Then
$$
\det\nolimits_\kappa(u_M) :
\det\nolimits_\kappa(M)
\longrightarrow
\det\nolimits_\kappa(M)
$$
is multiplication by $\overline{u}^l$ where $l = \text{length}_R(M)$
and $\overline{u} \in \kappa^*$ is the image of $u$.

\label{lemma-periodic-determinant-sign}
Let $R$ be a local ring with residue field $\kappa$.
Let $(M, \varphi, \varphi)$ be a $(2, 1)$-periodic complex over $R$.
Assume that $M$ has finite length and that $(M, \varphi, \varphi)$ is
exact. Then $\text{length}_R(M) = 2 \text{length}_R(\Im(\varphi))$
and
$$
\det\nolimits_\kappa(M, \varphi, \varphi)
=
(-1)^{\text{length}_R(\Im(\varphi))}
=
(-1)^{\frac{1}{2}\text{length}_R(M)}
$$
statement:

An admissible sequence is an $\ell$-tuple $(e_1,\ldots,e_\ell)$ with $\mathfrak m e_i\subseteq\sum_{j<i}Re_j$. The determinant line $\det_\kappa(M)$ is the $\kappa$-space generated by symbols $[e_1,\ldots,e_\ell]$ modulo: (i) a symbol is zero if any $e_i\in\sum_{j<i}Re_j$; (ii) replacing $e_i$ by $\lambda e_i'+x$ with $x\in\sum_{j<i}Re_j$ and $\lambda\in R^\times$ scales the symbol by $\bar\lambda$; (iii) exchanging adjacent $e_{i-1},e_i$ changes the sign when $\mathfrak m e_i\subseteq\sum_{j<i-1}Re_j$. This line is one-dimensional. An isomorphism $h:M\to N$ induces $\det_\kappa(h)$ by applying $h$ to admissible symbols. For a short exact sequence $0\to K\to L\to N\to0$, the canonical determinant isomorphism $\gamma_{K\to L\to N}:\det_\kappa K\otimes_\kappa\det_\kappa N\xrightarrow{\sim}\det_\kappa L$ concatenates an admissible sequence of $K$ with chosen lifts of one from $N$; it is natural under isomorphisms of exact sequences.

For finite-length $R$-module $M$ and endomorphisms $\varphi,\psi:M\to M$ with $\varphi\psi=\psi\varphi=0$ and $\ker\varphi=\operatorname{im}\psi$, $\ker\psi=\operatorname{im}\varphi$, call $(M,\varphi,\psi)$ an exact $(2,1)$-periodic complex. With $I_\varphi=\operatorname{im}\varphi$, $I_\psi=\operatorname{im}\psi$, put $K_\varphi=\ker\varphi=I_\psi$, $K_\psi=\ker\psi=I_\varphi$. Let $\gamma_\varphi:\det K_\varphi\otimes\det I_\varphi\to\det M$, $\gamma_\psi:\det K_\psi\otimes\det I_\psi\to\det M$ be the determinant isomorphisms and $\sigma$ swap the tensor factors. Define $\det_\kappa(M,\varphi,\psi)\in\kappa^\times$ as the unique scalar such that $\gamma_\psi\circ\sigma\circ\gamma_\varphi^{-1}$ acts on $\det M$ by $(-1)^{\ell(I_\varphi)\ell(I_\psi)}\det_\kappa(M,\varphi,\psi)$.

\label{lemma-pre-symbol}
Let $A$ be a Noetherian local ring.
Let $M$ be a finite $A$-module of dimension $1$.
Assume $\varphi, \psi : M \to M$ are two injective
$A$-module maps, and assume $\varphi(\psi(M)) = \psi(\varphi(M))$,
for example if $\varphi$ and $\psi$ commute.
Then $\text{length}_A(M/\varphi\psi M) < \infty$
and $(M/\varphi\psi M, \varphi, \psi)$ is an exact
$(2, 1)$-periodic complex.

\label{lemma-multiplicativity-symbol}
Let $A$ be a Noetherian local ring.
Let $a, b, c \in A$. Let $M$ be a finite $A$-module
with $\dim(\text{Supp}(M)) = 1$. Assume $a, b, c$ are nonzerodivisors on $M$.
Then
$$
d_M(a, bc) = d_M(a, b) d_M(a, c)
$$
and $d_M(a, b)d_M(b, a) = 1$.

\label{lemma-symbol-when-one-is-a-unit}
Let $A$ be a Noetherian local ring.
Let $M$ be a finite $A$-module of dimension $1$.
Let $b \in A$ be a nonzerodivisor on $M$, and let $u \in A^*$.
Then
$$
d_M(u, b) = u^{\text{length}_A(M/bM)} \bmod \mathfrak m_A.
$$

$d_A(u, b) = u^{\text{ord}_A(b)} \bmod \mathfrak m_A$.
